text: The goal of the archaeologists is to shed light on the daily life and environment of the past inhabitants of the Mosfell Valley. In order to understand the 1100 year period since the initial settlement, the Mosfell Archaeological Project (MAP) employs a holistic view of the whole valley and envisions this area as a functioning valley system made up of interlocking cultural and environmental pieces. The valley would have been a favorable place for the initial Viking Age settlers. The valley stretches from the highlands used for grazing and down to the sea that provided access to the rest of the Viking world. At the time of colonization there were abundant natural resources for the first inhabitants to utilize. The research aims to show how such a Norse society evolved from the beginning and hopes to provide insight into medieval mentality. The spotlight has been cast particularly on the farm of Hrísbrú where a longhouse, a church, and pagan and Christian graves have been unearthed.
